intro: This course covered food safety law, the 4 Cs, temperature control, allergens and Natasha's Law, plus supporting good nutrition and hydration in care.
points: There are 14 major allergens you must declare, and Natasha's Law means PPDS foods carry a full ingredients list — never guess.
Apply the 4 Cs every time — Cleaning, Cooking, Chilling and avoiding Cross-contamination — to keep food out of the danger zone.
Keep the fridge at 5C or below, cook and reheat food to a core temperature of 75C, and reheat only once.
Never use food after its use-by date, even if it looks and smells fine — use-by dates are about safety.
Wash hands thoroughly at the right moments, and never handle food until 48 hours after sickness or diarrhoea has stopped.
For dysphagia, follow the SALT-set IDDSI level exactly and never change texture or thickness yourself — the wrong one can cause choking.
